title: Finite-action economic MPC
body: Three-step horizon, replanned every five minutes
Maximize discounted PV production minus cap-change cost
Previous cap couples the decisions over time
Hard voltage and current constraints apply
foot: Five demand levels, eight actions and a shared 40-solve AC table
notes: Sources: Comparison_Lab.md and results/conventional records. MPC: https://sites.engineering.ucsb.edu/~jbraw/mpc/MPC-book-2nd-edition-4th-printing.pdf . DQN: https://www.nature.com/articles/nature14236 . Predictive safety filtering: https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.05506 . 59–62 min. Stage utility is PV_kW/8000 minus0.15 times absolute cap change/100. Discount0.95. Dynamic programming solves the finite horizon. Quasi-static power flow, no inverter or battery dynamics. Current ratings are held across the forecast horizon; no future event advance notice. Timing excludes table construction.

title: Three independently trained DQNs
foot: 18,000 transitions per seed, two hidden layers, replay and a target network
notes: Sources: Comparison_Lab.md and results/conventional records. MPC: https://sites.engineering.ucsb.edu/~jbraw/mpc/MPC-book-2nd-edition-4th-printing.pdf . DQN: https://www.nature.com/articles/nature14236 . Predictive safety filtering: https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.05506 . 62–65 min. The six inputs include demand forecast, previous cap, current rating and remaining episode fraction. Two48-unitReLU hidden layers. TD loss with Adam; no MPC labels. Nominal-rating training only. Exploration failures occur in simulation. Lower training violation rate is not a safety guarantee.

title: Fair safety comparisons
foot: Updated MPC is the matched-information deterministic counterfactual
notes: Sources: Comparison_Lab.md and results/conventional records. MPC: https://sites.engineering.ucsb.edu/~jbraw/mpc/MPC-book-2nd-edition-4th-printing.pdf . DQN: https://www.nature.com/articles/nature14236 . Predictive safety filtering: https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.05506 . 65–68 min. Four physical scenarios: two demand profiles, each nominal and transient. DRL has three training seeds; deterministic MPC repetitions are duplicates. Agents use one run per physical scenario and seed11 DQN. The Llama critic logs advice but does not revise routing in this experiment. Original search ablation tests critic value separately.

title: The shared safety layer explains the gain
foot: 12 simulated steps per episode. Rating falls to 80% during steps 5–8

All methods are safe in nominal episodes.

title: What the framework demonstrates
body: Correct constraints and checking explain the safety result
Language assists interpretation but can invent policy
Agents can coordinate MPC and learned tools
Engineering checks remain independent of model prose
foot: The measured result supports layered supervision, not universal controller superiority
notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 166–168 min. The practical result is repeatable, auditable decision support. Automation value could include operator workload reduction, but that requires a user study; it is not measured here.

title: Limits of the scientific evidence
body: One feeder and four constructed snapshots
Two seeds and handcrafted action catalogs
A sequential workflow with shared Llama weights
Simplified load relays and cyber evidence fixtures

notes: Sources: supplied tutorial proposal; SMART-DS https://data.openei.org/submissions/2981; experiment records in results/reference.json, benchmark.json, attacks.json and llama_calls.json. 168–170 min.
